newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ACCC says Wallis ambiguous on ACCC's jurisdiction.
newsitem.headline: ACCC says Wallis ambiguous on ACCC's jurisdiction.

text.p: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) chairman, Alan Fels said on Thursday the Wallis Inquiry into Australia's financial system was ambiguous in respect to the ACCC's role in protecting consumers in the event of a bank merger.
Asked whether the report suggested the Australian Securities Commission should be the sole regulator in this area, Fels said, "I think the report is a little ambiguous on that subject."

"The summary seems to say that, but if you actually read through the text it leaves it a good deal more open, and does seem to envisage concurrent jurisdiction (with the ASC) which is a solution we would tend to favour," Fels told reporters after a conference on media ownership.
Fels said the ACCC would be concerned if it was left with no role in applying the competition law in relation to the financial services sector.

"The main elements of the Wallis report on consumer protection are good and progressive. They represent a real step forward in sorting out the somewhat messy regulatory situation in that sector," he said.
The ACCC is currently considering Westpac Banking Corp's agreed bid for regional bank, Bank of Melbourne Ltd.
Fels earlier said the ACCC would take into account the recommendations of the Wallis report when considering the merger but this was not likely to change its view on the Westpac bid.
